hypothesis_text: Intraday candlestick shadow asymmetry (lab_shadow_imbalance_1h) reflects aggressive momentum exhaustion and passive liquidity absorption in perpetual futures across midcap altcoins (BNBUSDT, SOLUSDT, XRPUSDT). When absolute shadow imbalance exceeds 0.20, extreme upper shadows indicate aggressive buying absorbed at intraday highs (predicting downward reversal), while extreme lower shadows indicate aggressive selling absorbed at intraday lows (predicting upward reversal). This reversal effect is intensified when taker flow agrees with the rejected direction (gate_same_side on taker_buy_ratio_1h) due to trapped breakout traders facing liquidation or stop-out, and when orderbook resting depth is polarized (gate_tail on depth_imbalance_10).
narrative: In crypto perpetual futures markets, intraday price discovery frequently experiences momentum overextension driven by aggressive taker orders chasing short-term breakouts or breakdowns. The gene shadow_imbalance_1h measures the ratio of upper shadow minus lower shadow to total bar range over trailing 60 minutes. When shadow_imbalance_1h is strongly positive (> 0.20), price spiked towards session highs but failed to close near the top, leaving a prominent upper wick. This occurs when aggressive taker buying encounters resting limit ask walls and passive liquidity providers absorb the flow, causing momentum to stall. Chasing longs who entered near the peak become trapped underwater. As new buying fails to emerge, trapped longs are forced to cover or are stopped out, driving a mean-reverting price drop over subsequent 1h to 4h horizons. Symmetrically, when shadow_imbalance_1h is strongly negative (< -0.20), price dipped sharply but met resting bid absorption, leaving a long lower shadow; trapped short sellers are forced to buy back, prompting an upward rebound. The gate_same_side condition on taker_buy_ratio_1h captures the precise cohort where aggressive taker flow coincided with the wick creation: aggressive buyers at the top of an upper wick, or aggressive sellers at the bottom of a lower wick. In these instances, the volume of trapped liquidity is highest, producing a stronger and more reliable reversal edge. Conversely, gate_tail on depth_imbalance_10 isolates periods where resting orderbook depth was heavily asymmetric, confirming structural liquidity resistance that halts trend continuation.
research_rationale: Anchor candidate XL_midcap_alt_c65d444462f8 locks the two-sided predicate abs(shadow_imbalance_1h) > 0.20 on the midcap_alt basket (BNBUSDT, SOLUSDT, XRPUSDT). The predicate fired on 30,816 bars (24.89% panel match rate) spanning all 430 active scan days, with 13,355 episodes and 430 independent events. In T1 scoring projections, it achieved 421 scored days (projected 275 T1 days out of 281, clearing the 250-day floor). Shadow_imbalance_1h exhibits fast-decaying autocorrelation (0.776 at 1-bar, 0.066 at 1h, 0.016 at 1d), demonstrating that it is an intraday microstructure phenomenon rather than a slow macro state. Across individual symbols, quantile distributions are remarkably consistent (p95 is 0.274 on BNB, 0.262 on SOL, 0.260 on XRP), confirming no asset-specific scaling bias. The primary gene cemetery shows 0 prior trials for shadow_imbalance_1h (untested status), presenting an uncrowded research opportunity within the PRICE/MICRO family. For composition, taker_buy_ratio_1h was selected as the trigger partner: gate_same_side captures the economic core of trapped aggressive takers (2,920 candidate bars, projected 1,168 event observations at 60m). High and low controls (gate_high and gate_low) on taker_buy_ratio_1h are explicitly committed to separate the side-tied coupling from univariate taker share bias. Additionally, gate_tail on depth_imbalance_10 conditions on resting book asymmetry (1,735 candidate bars, projected 838 event observations). We chose search_scope='full' to explore both the committed gated interactions and automatic grid combinations across the three midcap assets. The predicted_sign is -1 (reversal on positive wicks, positive rebound on negative wicks).
